kept.title: A model that exits with code 0, 137 or 143 is recorded as “stopped” and never restarted; vLLM exits 0 when its engine dies
kept.scenario: A one-Spark vLLM model on the should-run list hits an engine error overnight. vLLM’s server then shuts itself down cleanly, exit code 0. The watcher records “stopped”, not “crashed”, so maybeHeal never runs, and the other heal pass leaves one-Spark models alone. The record says it stopped; the owner’s agents get errors until someone asks. It should count as a crash when nobody stopped it.
kept.wiring: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/19-watcher.mjs:102 (crashed = oomKilled, or an exit code other than 0, 137, 143) -> 19-watcher.mjs:103 (event 'stopped') -> 19-watcher.mjs:104 (maybeHeal only when crashed; it is the only caller) -> 20-heal.mjs:65 (healReason returns null for one-Spark entries unless the Spark was powered back on) -> 20-desired.mjs:50-54 (held, 'it isn’t running') -> 20-desired.mjs:82 (a notice, nothing restarts). Outside fact: vLLM's launcher sets server.should_exit = True in terminate_if_errored when the engine has died, and serve_http then returns normally (docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.11.0/api/vllm/entrypoints/launcher.html), so the process ends with 0; the exit code itself is inferred from that source, not observed. 137 is also what a kernel kill of the main process reports when Docker has not set OOMKilled. Related: when a crash is seen, 18-workflows.mjs:268-269 looks for 'out of memory' only in the last 80 log lines, which later tracebacks can push out.
kept.fix: In watchSpark, when a should-run container goes running→exited with 0/137/143 and consoleStopped has no entry for it in the last 15 minutes, read its last log lines: an engine-death or traceback line makes it “crashed” and goes to maybeHeal (its limits still apply); otherwise record “stopped outside Spark Console”.
kept.verifierNote: 19-watcher:102 counts exit 0, 137 and 143 as “stopped”; maybeHeal has no other caller and healReason:65 skips one-Spark entries, so the model is only held with a notice. vLLM’s launcher does set should_exit on engine death and return normally (docs checked); exit 0 is inferred, not observed. Two-Spark models take another path.
